messages:
incident-bot: [CRITICAL] KV cache paging spike detected on cluster aws-prod-gpu-pool (svc=text-gen). kv_cache_bytes increased 4.2x in 11m, paging events 520/min. Affected model variants: rwd/llama-2-13b-awq:v2, rwd/gptq-13b-int8:v1. Severity=P1. Paging routed to @sre_oncall. Alert ID INC-1939991234

sre_oncall: ack — I'm on it. Noted customer 5xx surge and tail-latency >5s for some routes. Starting triage. Can ml_infra join?

ml_infra: joining. Quick snapshot: continuous-batcher saw a shift in seq_len distribution -> average cached KV per req jumped ~3x. Kernel selector started choosing fallback kernel for AWQ int8 which doubles stored KV width (observed ~2x per-token footprint).

alice_h: any recent deploys to those model variants?

devon_ops: yes, auto-rollout last night pushed rwd/llama-2-13b-awq:v2 as preferred cheaper path for hosted. Canary looked fine with short sequences, but production has long-context chat usage.

ben_k: paste of the key log snippet from the runtime below:
```
2026-03-14T09:08:57Z runtime WARN kv_cache_manager.cpp:217 evict_pressure=0.72 cache_bytes=18.4GB max_cache=4.0GB
2026-03-14T09:09:02Z runtime ERROR batcher.cpp:544 failed_to_append batch_size=128 tokens=4096 reason=kv_memory_exceeded
2026-03-14T09:10:10Z perf INFO kernel_selector.cpp:102 selected_kernel=awq_fallback_nonopt kernel_kv_stride=64 kv_item_bytes=48
```

caroline_m: kernel_kv_stride=64 and kv_item_bytes=48 is the smoking gun — that matches the non-optimized AWQ kernel path. It stores a wider key/value layout.

pm_julia: immediate customer impact? CS please weigh in.

cs_tomas: two enterprise customers reporting errors: acmecorp-prod (high-volume chat) and medsys-eu (healthcare integration). Both seeing increased 500s and degraded throughput. Opening tickets.

sre_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) throttle requests to the affected model variants (soft throttle at proxy), 2) switch routing for heavy customers to stable gptq/int16 variants, 3) apply temporary batching cap to reduce max tokens per batch. I'll run steps 1 & 3 now.

devon_ops: commands I'm running now:
```
# soft throttle variant
curl -X POST "https://controlplane/api/v1/routes/variants/throttle" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"variant":"rwd/llama-2-13b-awq:v2","rate_limit_rps":30,"reason":"KV paging mitigation"}'

# reduce continuous-batcher max_batch_tokens
curl -X PATCH "https://controlplane/api/v1/configs/continuous-batcher" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"max_batch_tokens":1024,"max_batch_size":64}'
```

ml_infra: also flipping runtime flag to force kernel selector to prefer stable kernels (force_kernel_hint=gptq_fallback) for the AWQ variant while we investigate. This is a binary flag so it avoids full model rollback.

sre_oncall: throttle applied. Observability: paging events down to 60/min in last 3m, cache_bytes trending down from 18GB -> 6.2GB. Tail latency for affected routes moving from 5s -> ~1.2s. Customer 5xx rate has decreased but still above baseline.

ben_k: rolling change pushed for kernel hint to AWQ variant:
```
/opt/runtime/bin/runtime-admin set-model-flag --model rwd/llama-2-13b-awq:v2 --flag force_kernel_hint=gptq_fallback
```
Response: accepted, workers starting to rotate.

alice_h: do we have a long-term fix? Looks like AWQ int8 kernel selection is unstable with long seq_len distributions.

ml_infra: preliminary root cause: AWQ path's microkernel for our GPU arch triggers a slower but memory-hungry layout (kv stride increases for alignment), combined with continuous-batcher rising sequence lengths -> net KV footprint explosion. Two contributing issues: 1) kernel selector cost model underweights KV memory on long-seq workloads; 2) canary tests didn't exercise long context windows.

caroline_m: action items: update kernel selector scoring (weight KV footprint), add long-seq canary test, and add pre-deploy gate to reject AWQ variant if KV footprint > X per token in load tests.

pm_julia: we need customer comms. cs_tomas, can you draft an interim note informing impacted customers about mitigation and ETA for root-cause?

cs_tomas: on it. Draft: "We're mitigating a runtime kernel selection issue causing increased memory usage for some int8/awq variants. We've throttled the variant and routed you to a stable alternative; we're working on a permanent fix. We'll follow up within 4 hours with next steps."

devon_ops: monitoring: setting an automated rollback rule if cache_bytes > 8GB for any node for >5m. Hooked into deploy-bot so new rollouts will stop.

ben_k: quick metrics: before mitigation error-rate for text-gen-route=12.4% -> after throttles + kernel-hint -> 1.6% within 10m. Paging events dropped to 18/min and still falling.

sre_oncall: handing off to on-call for the next shift — I'll update incident doc and assign follow-ups. Main outstanding: kernel selector scoring change PR, long seq canary, and controlled rollout plan for AWQ v2.

alice_h: PR template for kernel selector patch (ml_infra + eng-runtime) — please include microbench for kv_item_bytes and a perf regression threshold on latency and cost.

ml_infra: ETA: patch for selector scoring today (3–4h), long-seq canary added to CI (tomorrow), and controlled rollout plan with 10% -> 50% -> 100% steps with telemetry checks.

pm_julia: estimated customer-facing timeline: low-risk fix + rollout ~24–48h, deeper kernel rewrite could take longer.

cs_tomas: sent interim notes to impacted customers (acmecorp-prod, medsys-eu). Both acknowledged and requested ETA; shared our mitigation steps.

caroline_m: postmortem pointers: capture exact kernel selection trace per request (we need more detailed tracing), and add a synthetic workload with long context to the model validation suite.

sre_oncall: incident status -> mitigated (paging under threshold, errors reduced). Severity will remain P2 until we complete selector fix and canary. Logging this thread to INC-1939991234 in incidents tracker.

devon_ops: leaving a config snapshot for on-call:
```
continuous-batcher max_batch_tokens=1024 max_batch_size=64
variant-throttle rwd/llama-2-13b-awq:v2=30rps
kernel_hint rwd/llama-2-13b-awq:v2=gptq_fallback
rollback-rule cache_bytes>8GB@5m -> disable-variant
```

ben_k: follow-ups assigned: @ml_infra update selector (PR #?), @eng-runtime add KV memory metric to kernel cost model, @devops add long-seq canary.

sre_oncall: final note: if you see cache_bytes trend back up >6GB or paging >50/min, re-escalate immediately. Closing handoff now — next on-call: @alice_h.

alice_h: acked, I'll monitor for the next 12h and coordinate the PR review. Good job team. :thumbsup
